task: Implement function-reachable project checking while retaining package validation in Margo.
observation: The first reachability probe exposed that checking by identifier mentions was too broad: a local variable or string literal could select an unrelated callable body. Switching the worklist to call-shaped syntax, with explicit handler message and known callback forms, avoided those false edges. The full regression then exposed that root main still depends on its concrete domain graph and that sort key callbacks are bare function references.
impact: Focused negative controls made the scope boundary auditable and caught two less-obvious edge classes before the C1 full regression is rerun.
evidence: make --jobs=16 check first run: 126/144 passed; 18 failures were reviewed from per-job logs

resolution.summary: Callback reachability is now driven by declared Callable parameter slots, including qualified identity; package-only duplicate/coherence cases remain behind Margo. See the focused shadowing and A.f/B.f tests.

suggestion: Keep a focused no-extra-diagnostics fixture beside reachability code, including local-name shadowing, strings/comments, callbacks, message handlers, and unrelated declarations.

task: Close C1 with a corpus-wide oracle comparing file diagnostics to reachable package diagnostics.
observation: The existing project checker and Margo build --check stop on the first CompileError and return a single structured error. That is enough to guard the 12 observed corpus changes, but it cannot enumerate all package diagnostics or prove that every reachable package diagnostic appears in a file check. The oracle requirement exposed this API limit before C1 could be marked complete.
impact: The 12-case gate is not a substitute for the requested all-diagnostic oracle; broader closeout must either provide diagnostic accumulation or explicitly define owner-isolated checks as the oracle unit.
evidence: src/moss.cpp: check_project_sources catches and rethrows one CompileError
margo: build --check stops on the first target failure

resolution.summary: The Bank replaced diagnostic-set enumeration with fail-fast G-a/G-b implications and explicitly kept multi-error reporting out of scope. The oracle-only checker changes were removed; see C1_RESULTS.md.

task: Run a full source-corpus diagnostic-set oracle for C1 file and package checks.
observation: The oracle visited the 2,064-source corpus but completed only 2,029 paired or standalone file checks across 519 package target queries; 35 source rows were not verified. It reported 675 package/terminal diagnostics and 28 uncomparable rows: 16 internal checker errors, four signal-11 exits, six package/file differences in stale dependency interfaces, one malformed fixture package graph, and one file diagnostic absent from package output. Targeted checks passed for the Calc and Toolkit C1 fixtures but do not establish corpus-wide parity.
impact: C1 cannot receive Architect GO or proceed to T1 until the 35 unchecked sources and 28 uncomparable rows are resolved or the acceptance contract explicitly handles them. Treating internal failures or differing dependency errors as equivalent would mask missing-diagnostic risks.
evidence: MOSS_INTERNAL_OR_IO_ERROR: unresolved concrete method effect target
MOSS_COMPILE_ERROR: interface for dsu is missing or stale

resolution.summary: This historical experiment is not the accepted C1 gate. Fail-fast G-a/G-b now pass over the tracked corpus; known internal/crash cases were checked against main and documented separately. See docs/phase26/C1_RESULTS.md.

tool_used: moss --phase26-c1-oracle --json; Margo package graph and check mode

task: Check that file-scoped reachability preserves callbacks passed across package interfaces.
observation: The corpus G-a gate found that `moss check <file>` omitted `LogAnalytics.is_slow_request` when it was passed as a named argument to generic `DataTools.filter_by` from an imported `.mossi` API. Package check accepted both files, while file checks rejected with `TYPE_INFERENCE_FAILED`. The call syntax alone did not show the function-reference edge; the formal callable constraint in the imported signature identifies the argument slot.
impact: Without this edge, file-scoped checking can reject code that package checking accepts. Reproducing the case in the real package provided a focused regression while keeping ordinary value arguments out of scope.

resolution.summary: Reachability now traces declared function references only at call argument positions marked Callable by the callee signature, and the corpus gate checks every accepted-package source.

suggestion: Keep callback arguments and same-name ordinary values as paired scope tests.

task: Audit corpus package discovery against Margo's manifest-root rules.
observation: The C1 corpus gate searched for `Moss.toml` only, while Margo's nearest-project lookup and manifest loader also recognize lowercase `moss.toml`. It therefore reported 421 roots instead of the 438 present in the tracked corpus and skipped both `examples/priority_queue` and `examples/swarm/Julia/CircularBuffer`, which had accepted-to-rejected identity regressions. Updating discovery to walk from each source to its nearest ancestor containing either manifest spelling made the pre-fix gate fail on both roots and the post-fix gate pass over 438 roots.
impact: A passing corpus gate did not cover all package projects. Matching the production manifest-root lookup is necessary for the reachability implications to cover the repository's actual package set.

resolution.summary: The gate now walks nearest ancestors and recognizes both manifest spellings; final G-a is 654/654 and G-b is 70/70 over 438 roots.

suggestion: Share package-root discovery with Margo or test both manifest spellings in every corpus gate.
